items.briefing:
Cybercriminals are now using calendar invitation files (.ics) to deliver phishing attacks — a tactic flagged by Barracuda this week. These malicious invites can appear in your inbox looking like legitimate meeting requests, but clicking links within them may compromise your account or device. This is particularly relevant as calendar tools are widely used across training organisations for scheduling classes, meetings, and events.

**Practical tip:** If you receive an unexpected calendar invite — especially from an unknown sender — don't click any links inside it. Delete it and verify with the sender directly through a separate channel.
